issues.description: New command names break the file's singular-dash convention (quickmark-* / bookmark-*).
issues.detail: Existing commands are :quickmark-save, :quickmark-load, :bookmark-add, :bookmark-load — singular. The patch adds :quickmarks-reload and :bookmarks-reload (plural). All three reviewers flagged this as the headline problem. Either rename to the singular form or justify the break in the commit message; do not introduce a second naming rule in the same file.

issues.description: reload() has no failure invariant and silently emits changed from __init__.
issues.detail: reload() calls self.marks.clear() then re-parses. If parsing raises mid-reload, marks is left empty while the on-disk file is intact and no signal is emitted. Routing __init__ through reload() also fires changed during construction, altering the constructor's postcondition. Build the new dict first, swap atomically, emit once, and document or suppress the construction-time signal.

issues.description: reload() silently discards unsaved in-memory marks and races with the save manager.
issues.detail: Reload clears marks without checking dirty state, and the emitted changed signal will mark the save-manager dirty and round-trip the freshly loaded contents back to disk. For a manually invoked command this may be acceptable, but the docstring should state 'discards unsaved changes' and the autosave interaction should be reasoned about rather than discovered later.

issues.description: Unit test only covers BookmarkManager replacement; quickmark path and clear-on-reload contract untested.
issues.detail: test_reload exercises BookmarkManager rewriting one URL to another. It never runs QuickmarkManager.reload() (which overrides _parse_line), never verifies removed entries are dropped, and does not assert the pre-reload state to prove __init__ actually loaded. Add a quickmark case and a removed-entry assertion to lock the contract.

issues.description: New end-to-end scenarios are unnamed and only assert the info message.
issues.detail: Both Gherkin scenarios start with bare 'Scenario:' while every other scenario in the file has a descriptive title. They also only check that the user-visible message appears — they do not mutate the on-disk file between writes and assert the in-memory marks changed. Name them and assert the actual reload effect.

issues.description: Two near-identical command bodies; consider splitting the patch or extracting a helper.
issues.detail: quickmarks_reload and bookmarks_reload are six lines each, identical except for registry key and message. Either factor out a _reload_marks(name, label) helper to make the duplication explicit, or split the two command additions into separate patches so each can be bisected and reverted independently on top of the shared reload() refactor.

synthesis.summary: Consensus: NEEDS-WORK but salvageable. The reviewers agree the core refactor — folding __init__'s parse loop into a reusable reload() on UrlMarkManager — is the right shape and should land. The headline problem, flagged unanimously, is that the new command names (:quickmarks-reload / :bookmarks-reload) break the file's established singular-dash convention. Beyond naming, reload() lacks a stated failure invariant, silently discards unsaved state, and now emits 'changed' during construction. Tests are minimal: the QuickmarkManager path is uncovered, the clear-on-reload contract is not asserted, and the feature scenarios are unnamed and only check the info message.
